target_customer: Residential and small commercial general contractors, home builders, remodelers and roofers
problem: Contractors run estimates, plans, proposals, photos, permits and change orders across disconnected tools, so admin work eats time that should go to jobs.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for contractors, with a 30 day trial that needs a card up front
product_category: AI construction project management and estimating software

founders.name: Nolan Rossi
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as the founder. A fetch summary attributed a bio (Berkeley M.E.T. program, Amazon engineer, family construction business) to a separate Scout Out launch post that was not opened, so it is not recorded here.

competitors.name: Buildertrend
competitors.what: Incumbent all in one construction management suite for builders and remodelers
competitors.traction_then: Established incumbent; roundups describe its estimating and takeoffs as manual

competitors.name: JobTread
competitors.what: Construction management and estimating platform positioned as a Buildertrend alternative
competitors.traction_then: Established product; a vendor comparison says its takeoff relies on manual measurement and AI is via third party connections

technical_complexity.rationale: A broad CRUD suite plus AI takeoff from plan sets and QuickBooks two way sync. Plan reading with LLMs was feasible for a small team in 2026 but accuracy on drawings is hard.

defensibility.rationale: Once a contractor keeps customer records, documents and job history in one system there is some lock in, but AI estimating features are easy for incumbents and rivals such as Handoff AI to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known as of late 2026. Vendor comparison pages show rivals marketing AI takeoff, and JobTread has added third party AI connections.

market_need_then: The company cites contractors working across estimates in spreadsheets, plans in email and photos on phones. Third party review sites list many competing contractor tools, which shows spend exists. No quantified demand figure was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses foreman.co, not the .com. A separate older product named Contractor Foreman (contractorforeman.com) shares the name.

identity.logo: Orange and white logo versions on the site
identity.visual_style: Not described in sources beyond orange and white
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain trade language, tagline Keeping contractors on the job site, not behind a desk

brand_strength.rationale: A fitting trade word that signals the audience, but search results mix it up with Contractor Foreman and no press on the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Foreman is a Winter 2026 company and is still active as of November 2026 with no reported exit, layoffs or shutdown. The founder describes a construction family background in unopened material, which may give domain fit, but no funding, revenue or user figures are public. It faces entrenched suites that are adding AI, so the main open question is whether AI takeoff quality wins contractors.
notes: Searches found no funding announcement. Third party pages say team size 2 while the YC listing says 6. Customer logos on the site are self reported. No outcome news found; searches mostly surfaced Contractor Foreman, a different company.
